profile.headline: Engineer, Intrinsic at Google
profile.summary:
Engineering Philosophy: Create value for customers systemically by supporting developer velocity and impact. 

I focus on QA strategy, execution, and impact. 

Engineering, Robotics, Software. 

becschwartz.com
hello@becschwartz.com

positions.title: Software Engineer Technical Lead
positions.description:
Technical Lead for Intrinsic’s Product Quality (QA) Group. 

Deliver quality releases to customers.

positions.title: Software Engineer III
positions.description:
I focus on QA automation, tooling, and strategy. 

Philosophy driving strategy, action: 
1. Bring egregious bugs from -have to cherry pick on our release branch to fix- to -avoided in presubmit- 
2. Testing is hard. Focus on writing tests that if failing, are most likely failing due to a release-blocking bug. 
3. Make the work done by other devs useful for QA and release process.
(1) if the tests they write are important for a customer, make sure we run it on our release candidate
(2) make use of tooling provided by other devs

Key achievements:
1. My monitor-release-tests policy prevents our release from being blocked
- my policy allows me to find and report bugs that will block our next release candidate if unfixed to (1) prevent devs from building on top of the bug, and (2) avoid complex + time consuming cherry-picks from being required in a release. 
- I wrote some of the tests which I monitor, which have both caught and prevented release-blocking bugs. 
- these tests make use of developer efforts of writing post-submit tests which, if failing, may be due to an otherwise uncaught release blocking bug. 

2. QA automation 
I’ve automated many tests which catch and prevent release-blocking bugs. I’m continuing to automate testing. 

3. I get tests running on our release candidate. 
I started the effort and am continuing the effort to ensure tests which can catch release-blocking bugs are being run directly on our release candidate. 
I’ve achieved this with: google tooling, GitHub actions. 

What I’m known for: 
1. Getting robots running automated tests daily, and running robots in general 
2. Catching motion-based regressions. 
3. QA strategy & action

positions.title: Robotics Performance Engineer II
positions.description:
Wrote the first hardware in the loop test to catch regressions in our product; the test has caught numerous bugs in our motion stack, which otherwise would have caused our robot motion execution time to more than double. 
My documentation for writing hardware in the loop tests has helped other engineers write their own tests, to further catch regressions. 
Acted as Engr PM to help deliver our product’s keynote video to YouTube. 
PM’d for QA for our early access program launch. 
PMing for Intrinsic for external sim and hw workflow testing with Ekumen, leading to significant UX improvements in our product. 
Helping improve QA efficiency and effectiveness to improve product reliability and end user experience. 


Vicarious has been acquired by Alphabet’s Intrinsic as of May 2022.

positions.title: Robotics Performance Engineer II
positions.description:
• Leading QA for Vicarious’ largest in-development packaging project using AI and Kuka Robots to pick and place in an unstructured environment
- Wrote the verification matrix based off of internal and external requirements, and detailed test methods and cases
- Diagnose bugs through testing and work with respective engineering teams to ensure bug-fixes are adequate
- Identified risks and offered mitigation strategies during early stage development, which is shaping the project
- Adjusting test methods and strategies in real-time along with changing customer requirements
• Designed and implemented release test verification for kitting and packaging projects, ensuring bug-free software releases
• Leading QA for a secondary kitting project; diagnosing bugs as they arise in our Latest master branch
• Using ROS, git and github in a linux environment to run robots to perform regression, AB, integration, and bisect testing

positions.title: Quality And Reliability Engineer
positions.description:
- Lead reliability engineer for Kawasaki Robotics' #1 priority project for new flagship silicon-wafer handling robot in R&D phase
      Write and carry out testing involving laser tracker, accelerometer, Keyence lasers
      Build and use jigs for testing 
- Perform QA (quality assurance) to ensure the physical health of silicon-wafer handling robots
- Perform regression tests to ensure that new and updated robotics software is bug-free for customers
- Perform FA (failure analyses) on customer robots and associated equipment
      Perform tests to diagnose robot then fix issue
      Write detailed reports for customer; keep customer informed; lead and carry out corrective and preventative actions
- Tune robots to minimize vibration, acceleration, while maximizing silicon-wafer throughput

positions.title: Mechatronics Engineering Intern
positions.description:
Future-proof code for centrally actuated tensegrity mobile robot I built during Capstone project
      Take into consideration potential future design choices that may be made for next robot iteration
Assemble next generation flagship tensegrity mobile robot, MR3 
     Assembly of all electro-mechanical components
     Dremel, epoxy, crimping for all structural components
Saw MR3 project through -- worked to enable MR3's first "steps".... the first time in over a year that the company produced tensegrity mobile robot motion

positions.title: Mechatronics Engineering Intern
positions.description:
• Led hardware assembly to build Squishy Robotics’ first centrally actuated tensegrity mobile robot 
• Enabled face-to-face motor control using Dijkstra’s shortest path algorithm and an IMU  
• Hired as a full time Mechatronics Engineering Intern for May – Aug 2020

positions.title: Mechanical Engineer Co-op
positions.description:
Designed mechanical and plumbing building systems using fluid mechanics and thermodynamics
Drafted plumbing, fire protection, and mechanical systems for 10 projects in Revit

positions.title: Formulations Engineering Co-op
positions.description:
Engineering co-op for Agricultural Solutions Division 

Managed front end of $400k project to upgrade and relocate an insecticide packaging line	
Designed and implemented a scheme to minimize a biological cleanout’s water usage by 42%
Created models in Engineers Aide SiNET to analyze flow and pressure for a mill integration project
Analyzed financial data from SAP using advanced Excel functions

positions.title: Project Manager
positions.description:
Led a $49,000 mechanical project to renovate a Variable Air Volume system
-completed phase 1 of construction
Presented need for new piping systems after processing 268 pages of ultrasonic testing data in Excel 
Managed paperwork & permits, and kept stakeholders informed for four projects simultaneously 
The 4 projects: replacing fill for cooling towers; energy savings project; VAV system in office area; ultrasonic testing 
Processed pressure and temperature data for presentation to the Joint Commission (JCAHO) which provides accreditation for hospitals

positions.title: Undergraduate Biomechanics Research Assistant
positions.description:
Assisted a research team to advance the understanding of the biomechanics of running
Processed data collected in the Gait Lab using Visual 3D and Excel for PhD students
Test piloted 3 studies to help improve research methods

positions.title: Taekwondo Instructor
positions.description:
Taught students ages 6-70 years old the art, practice, philosophy, and history of Taekwondo
Tailored instruction based on student’s goals, which include healthy living, learning discipline, and mastering the art
Facilitated a summer camp in July 2012, leading twenty (20) 7-year-old students
Planned and led detailed child and adult classes
Worked with students with disabilities by taking appropriate measures specific to each student's needs
Acted as a judge at belt testings

positions.title: Volunteer Taekwondo Instructor
positions.description:
Learned teaching methods, preframing and reframing communication style, and how to use positive reinforcement
Passed instructor training course, hired as a Taekwondo instructor

Completed 150 Community Action Service hours

projects.title: Feedback Control with Optical Shaft Encoders
projects.description:
Built a 2R robot to demonstrate feedback control using optical shaft encoders and Arduino UNO 
Coded and wired Arduino UNO in C++

__Project URL__
See page 2 of paper for links to YouTube demonstrations

projects.title: Balance Inverted Pendulum using LQR
projects.description:
Designed a linear quadratic regulator (LQR) in MATLAB to balance a 2R inverted pendulum

__Project URL__
See document for write-up of experiment

organizations.name: Drexel Honors Student Advisory Committee
organizations.description:
Drexel's Honors Student Advisory Committee (HSAC) promotes diversity and inclusion on campus by hosting a wide range of events which are subsidized by the university. 

Duties as President: Oversee member training, event planning, and treasury activities 
In addition to regular duties: I worked with Drexel German Club's president for six months to plan and lead HSAC's biggest event ever. 

Prior to serving as president: I served as associate treasurer, cultural affairs director, and then vice president
